record.paper_title: Recent progress and open questions on the numerical index of Banach spaces
record.context_brief: Polynomial numerical index of c_0 and ℓ_∞ sums
record.original_question: Let {X_λ} be a family of complex Banach spaces. Determine whether n^(k)([⊕_λ X_λ]_{c_0}) = n^(k)([⊕_λ X_λ]_{ℓ_∞}) = inf_λ n^(k)(X_λ).

evidence.quote: Problem 38. Let {Xλ : λ ∈ Λ} be a family of complex Banach spaces. Is it true that n(k)([⊕λ∈ΛXλ]c0 ) = n(k)([⊕λ∈ΛXλ]ℓ∞ ) = infλ n(k)(Xλ) ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a complex Banach space $X$ and an integer $k\ge 1$, let $\mathcal{P}(^kX;X)$ denote the space of continuous $k$-homogeneous polynomials $P:X\to X$ endowed with the sup norm $\|P\|=\sup\{\|P(x)\|:\|x\|\le 1\}$, and define the numerical radius
$$v(P)=\sup\{|x^*(P(x))| : x\in X,\ x^*\in X^*,\ \|x\|=\|x^*\|=x^*(x)=1\}.$$
The polynomial numerical index of order $k$ of $X$ is
$$n^{(k)}(X)=\inf\{v(P): P\in\mathcal{P}(^kX;X),\ \|P\|=1\}.$$

Given a family $\{X_\lambda:\lambda\in\Lambda\}$ of complex Banach spaces, form the $c_0$- and $\ell_\infty$-sums
$$\Big[\bigoplus_{\lambda\in\Lambda}X_\lambda\Big]_{c_0},\qquad \Big[\bigoplus_{\lambda\in\Lambda}X_\lambda\Big]_{\ell_\infty}.$$

Determine whether, for every such family and every integer $k\ge 2$,
$$n^{(k)}\!\Big(\Big[\bigoplus_{\lambda\in\Lambda}X_\lambda\Big]_{c_0}\Big)=n^{(k)}\!\Big(\Big[\bigoplus_{\lambda\in\Lambda}X_\lambda\Big]_{\ell_\infty}\Big)=\inf_{\lambda\in\Lambda}n^{(k)}(X_\lambda).$$
artifact.category_tag: Polynomial numerical index of Banach spaces
artifact.status_search_result: Searches turned up related work on polynomial numerical indices and on numerical indices of absolute sums (where the analogous equality for the numerical index n(·) and c_0/ℓ_∞-sums is known), but no source clearly settles the polynomial (k≥2) version for arbitrary families of complex Banach spaces. The status of this specific equality could not be definitively verified.

status_evidence.title: The polynomial numerical index of a Banach space
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces and studies the polynomial numerical index n^(k) of Banach spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Background definitions for the polynomial numerical index.

status_evidence.title: Numerical index of absolute sums of Banach spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Studies when the numerical index of an absolute sum is at most the infimum of the numerical indices, with equality in the ℓ_∞-sum case.
status_evidence.claim: Related result for the (non-polynomial) numerical index of c_0/ℓ_∞-sums; does not establish the polynomial case in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Banach spaces with polynomial numerical index 1
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizes spaces with polynomial numerical index 1 under the Radon-Nikodým property.
status_evidence.claim: Related but does not resolve the c_0/ℓ_∞-sum equality for polynomial numerical indices.
